summary: Converts CHOP channel values into DAT table rows or columns so channel data can be inspected, serialized, scripted, or joined with other DAT workflows.

key_params.name: chop
key_params.note: CHOP path used as the source of channel values

key_params.name: names
key_params.note: Include an additional column or row with channel names

key_params.name: latestsample
key_params.note: Use only the latest sample when the source CHOP is time sliced

key_params.name: output
key_params.note: Choose row-per-channel or column-per-channel output layout

key_params.name: language
key_params.note: Common DAT language setting for editor/script context

key_params.name: extension
key_params.note: Edit/view file extension exposed to external editors

key_params.name: customext
key_params.note: Custom editor extension when Extension is set to Custom Extension

key_params.name: wordwrap
key_params.note: Common DAT node-display word wrap setting

common_gotchas: When the source is time sliced, leaving latestsample off can make the DAT table size change as frame timing changes.
Row-per-channel and column-per-channel layouts imply different lookup expressions; choose deliberately before downstream DAT logic depends on cell positions.
The CHOP parameter is an explicit source path, so generated networks should reference a stable Null CHOP instead of a volatile upstream node.
This is a table conversion, not a resampling operator; fix CHOP sample rates and channel scope before converting to DAT.
key_concepts: Converts CHOP channel samples into a DAT table.
Can include channel names as an output row or column.
Latest Sample keeps time-sliced CHOP input from changing the table size every cook.
Output orientation determines whether channels become rows or columns.
